_purpose: Field detail for the three layout-engine tables that /en/admin/ShowObjectDetails.jsp refuses to describe ('Data for that table not supported'). These are the tables ASG Edge+ needs to rebuild its layout engine.
_evidence: Observed. Recovered from the REST serializer, GET /rest/businessObject/PageLayout/lxid/{id}?deep=true, across 134 of the tenant's 135 layouts. Corroborated against the admin edit forms.
_whyNotInObjectCatalog: docs/data-model/object-catalog.md derives from ShowObjectDetails output, so every table that viewer refuses is absent from the catalog by construction, not by oversight. 25 of the 227 tables are refused; the layout trio is among them.

recoveryMethod.primary: GET /rest/businessObject/PageLayout/lxid/{pageLayoutID}?deep=true&wantClientID=true returns the PageLayout record with its PageLayoutField children fully serialised. Column names in that JSON are the physical column names.
corroboration: GET /en/pagebuilder/SummaryEntityPageLayoutEdit.jsp?mode={SEP|SUB|LIST}&formSubmit=editBO&popupEdit=true&BOID={id} - the edit form's input names are PageLayout columns.

GET /en/reports/CustomReportFieldEdit.jsp?popupEdit=true&formSubmit=editBO&update=true&BOType=CustomObjectDel&CustomObjectDelID={cellHash}&showDateFields=true - the field-properties form; its inputs are PageLayoutField columns and json.* sub-keys.
recoveryMethod.caveat: The REST serializer emits only columns that are POPULATED on the records sampled, so these lists are a lower bound on the physical schema. Foreign keys serialise as reference objects {'#text','@lxID','@clientID','@href'} rather than raw integers.

notes: CodeIssueTypeID is what makes a PageLayout a FORM layout - it binds the layout to an Issue Type. Summary/sub/list layouts leave it null.
PageLayoutType and OutputType are single-character discriminators (observed 'V' and 'L' on a summary layout).

ParentPageLayoutID is self-referential. PreviousPageLayoutID is a second self-reference and is a SEQUENCE pointer - it orders sibling layouts within one navigation node, e.g. Abstract Details -> CAM -> Delivery Requirements -> Funds and Expenses -> Real Estate Taxes. CORRECTED 2026-09-13: this note previously read 'used for versioning/duplication', which was my inference from the column NAME alone and was wrong.

JSONConfigText is a serialised JSON blob - this is the physical home of every 'json_*' input seen on the edit form. 87 of 134 layouts carry a non-empty one; observed keys: AssetID_LimitBy, AssetList_LimitBy, SL_LimitBy, NoGridWidths.
RunModeFilters and EntitySelectionFilter are integer bitmasks.

Geometry is stored as three parallel coordinate sets - Edit*, View* and Header* - so one row positions the field differently in edit, view and header contexts. EditRowPosition / EditColumnPosition / EditFieldWidth / EditFieldHeight, and the View* equivalents; -1 means 'not placed in that context'.
ReportGroupAvailableFieldID is the FK to the data-field catalogue (RGAF); it is the 'fieldKey' used by ConditionFilterEx.jsp. Pseudo-fields use it too: StaticText, OneToManyList.
SubPageLayoutID lets a field embed another PageLayout - this is how sub-pages attach.
DisplayOption1 / DisplayOption2 are integer bitmasks (observed 0 and 288).
JSONConfigText is the per-field JSON blob and is where conditionalFieldsConfig lives.
StaticText and FieldContext appear only on the field types that use them.

evidence: It is a valid REST record type - it appears in GET /rest/firm/types alongside PageLayout and PageLayoutField.
GET /rest/businessObject/PageLayoutFilter returns {"businessObjectLinks":[]} - zero records in the tenant.
No PageLayoutFilter child array appeared on any of the 134 layouts deep-serialised.
PageLayoutFilter.conclusion: Its columns cannot be recovered from BBW because the tenant holds no rows and the serializer emits only populated columns. Blocked, not guessed. To recover it, deep-serialise a PageLayout from a tenant that uses run-mode filters, or read PageLayout.RunModeFilters (an integer bitmask, 0 on every BBW layout) which is the flag that would drive filter rows.

relatedRefusedTables.note: Also refused. Reachable as a REST type.
Refused by ShowObjectDetails but present in GET /rest/firm/types.

crossCheck: The REST type list (GET /rest/firm/types) returns exactly 227 names, matching the 227 sqlTableID options one-for-one - including all 25 that ShowObjectDetails refuses. So the REST layer is the better census source for those 25.

_CORRECTION_previousPageLayoutID.was: PreviousPageLayoutID is a second self-reference used for versioning/duplication.
_CORRECTION_previousPageLayoutID.now: PreviousPageLayoutID is a sequence pointer that orders sibling layouts within a single navigation node.
_CORRECTION_previousPageLayoutID.evidence: kb-builder joined the Previous Layout pairs listed by Export Configuration against the layout registry: 8 of 8 chained pairs share a navigation parent, and every multi-layout node resolves to exactly one ordered chain. Observed, by kb-builder, not by me.
_CORRECTION_previousPageLayoutID.whyIWasWrong: I read the meaning off the column name - 'Previous' suggested a prior version - without testing it against what the pairs actually link. The chains link semantically distinct layouts in a reading order, not successive versions of one layout. Same failure mode as the label-vs-physical-name census diff and the 'only 0 and 288' note: a confident reading from a convenient signal instead of the data.
